_comment: Golden cases for the foreign-issuer classifier (Tool 1). See README.md in this folder.
EVERY CASE IS PROVISIONAL: verified_by is null - nobody at the bank has checked a code against
CTS. Scoring reports verified and provisional separately, and no accuracy figure may be quoted
Two kinds of case. The ten fictional ones (source 'fictional') each trap one known pre-filter
failure with a controlled text. The real ones (roadmap E8, 22 Sept 2026) are foreign issuers of
the kinds MO sets up, researched from public sources (GLEIF, OpenFIGI, ESMA FIRDS, issuer reports,
the ECB lists) and re-checked by an independent reviewer; each carries its ISIN, the reasoning,
the alternatives and the evidence. ESA codes come from CNB BA0036 version 044; the control axis is
judged from the issuer's own country (roadmap Q7) - see depends_on_q7.
To verify a case: check it against CTS, then fill in verified_by and verified_on.

cases.description: Special purpose funding vehicle of the Nordkap banking group. Issues bonds on international markets and on-lends the proceeds exclusively to its parent bank and that bank's subsidiaries. Does not take deposits from the public and holds no banking licence of its own.
cases.note: The core trap: the group name contains 'Bank' and the entity issues bank-like paper, but it is a captive finance vehicle, not a bank. Distinguishing 2002703 from 2002213 is the whole point of the ESA half.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Účelová finanční společnost skupiny Nordkap Bank. Vydává dluhopisy na mezinárodních trzích a získané prostředky půjčuje výhradně mateřské bance a jejím dceřiným společnostem. Nepřijímá vklady od veřejnosti a nemá vlastní bankovní licenci.
cases.note: Same case in Czech. Pairs with captive-funding-spv to measure how much the pre-filter loses when the description is not in the codebook's language.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: German manufacturer of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles, operating three assembly plants. Majority owned by a foreign automotive group. Issues bonds to finance its own operations.
cases.note: No financial vocabulary at all. Exists because an early version of the pre-filter returned zero ESA candidates here: the residual sector 'Nefinanční podniky' has to be reachable without a keyword hit.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Italian commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Italy, taking retail and corporate deposits and providing loans. Wholly owned by a French banking group.
cases.note: The straightforward bank, and the control axis: foreign-owned, so 2002213 rather than 2002212.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Swiss non-life insurance undertaking writing property and casualty business, subsidiary of a foreign insurance group.
cases.note: NACE 65 covers insurance and pension funding together; ESA separates insurers from pension funds.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Irish designated activity company established to acquire a portfolio of residential mortgage loans and fund the purchase by issuing rated asset-backed notes. No employees and no activity beyond holding the portfolio.
cases.note: Must land on the securitisation sector 2002513 rather than the generic captive 2002703 - both are 'special purpose' entities in ordinary language.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Provides finance leases and instalment credit for commercial vehicles and machinery to business customers. Funded by bank facilities and bond issues. Subsidiary of a foreign industrial group.
cases.note: Lender rather than captive: it lends to third parties, not only within its group.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Luxembourg open-ended investment company investing in listed European equities on behalf of institutional investors. Not a money market fund.
cases.note: Explicitly not a money market fund, so 2002403 rather than 2002303.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Multilateral development bank owned by member states, financing infrastructure projects in its member countries. Enjoys preferred creditor status and is exempt from national banking supervision.
cases.note: A supranational is neither a resident nor an ordinary foreign bank; it has its own ESA sector. A pre-filter that only knows the word 'bank' will get this wrong.
cases.source: fictional

cases.description: Operates a chain of supermarkets and convenience stores across several European countries. Listed on Euronext.
cases.note: A second non-financial issuer, with the word 'Holdings' in the name to check that it does not drag the answer towards a holding-company classification.
cases.source: fictional

cases.instrument: Bund 2.60% 15 Aug 2033, EUR 30.5bn fixed-rate federal bond (FIRDS CFI DBFTFB; OpenFIGI DBR 2.6 08/15/33, Govt)
cases.description: Federal Republic of Germany, borrowing at central (federal) government level. Its debt management office, Bundesrepublik Deutschland - Finanzagentur GmbH in Frankfurt, a company wholly owned by the Federation, issues federal securities such as Bunds, Bobls, Schätze and Bubills on the Federation's behalf to finance the federal budget.
cases.nace_reasoning: Issuing debt is the state financing itself, which NACE treats as general public administration: class 84.11 explicitly covers budget implementation and management of public funds and public debt, including raising money (explanatory notes of NACE Rev. 2, p. 288, and Rev. 2.1). The Finanzagentur is only the agent; the issuer is the Federation itself, so 64/66 (financial services) would describe the agent, not the issuer. Division 84 in both Rev. 2 (section O) and Rev. 2.1 (section P).
cases.esa_reasoning: ESA 2010 S.1311 central government: the Bund is Germany's federal (central) level, recorded by GLEIF as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY / CENTRAL_GOVERNMENT. Non-resident BA0036 leaf 2003110 'Ústřední vládní instituce' (verified in ČNB SDAT BA0036 v044; described as analogous to resident 1311000). Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.
cases.note: Trap: FIRDS names the issuer 'BUNDESREPUBLIK DEUTSCHLAND - FINANZAGENTUR GMBH' and GLEIF gives a c/o Finanzagentur GmbH address, so a name-based classifier may treat the issuer as a limited company (public corporation 2001001 or auxiliary 2002601, NACE 66/70). The GmbH is only the debt agent; the issuer is the sovereign.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.instrument: RAGB 2.90% 23 May 2029, EUR 7.6bn fixed-rate federal government bond (FIRDS CFI DBFTFB; OpenFIGI RAGB 2.9 05/23/29, Govt)
cases.description: Republic of Austria as a sovereign borrower at federal (central government) level. Its debt management office, the Austrian Treasury (OeBFA) in Vienna, borrows for the Republic's account, issuing Austrian government bonds (RAGB), treasury bills, commercial paper and EMTN notes to fund the federal budget and refinance maturing debt.
cases.nace_reasoning: Issuing debt is the state financing itself, which NACE treats as general public administration: class 84.11 explicitly covers budget implementation and management of public funds and public debt, including raising money (explanatory notes of NACE Rev. 2, p. 288, and Rev. 2.1). OeBFA is the debt office acting for the Republic; the issuer is the federal state. Division 84 in both Rev. 2 and Rev. 2.1.
cases.esa_reasoning: ESA 2010 S.1311 central government (the Bund level of Austria); GLEIF: RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY / CENTRAL_GOVERNMENT. BA0036 non-resident leaf 2003110 'Ústřední vládní instituce' (verified, ČNB SDAT v044). The ELF 'Körperschaft öffentlichen Rechts' is a legal form of public-law bodies, not a sign of a public corporation. Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.
cases.note: Trap: the GLEIF legal form reads 'public-law corporation' and the address is that of the OeBFA debt office, which can push a classifier towards 'veřejné podniky' (2001001) or an auxiliary financial unit; the RAGB issuer is the Republic, i.e. central government.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.issuer: United States of America (U.S. Department of the Treasury)
cases.instrument: U.S. Treasury note 3.375% 15 Sep 2028, USD 58.0bn fixed-rate 3-year note (FIRDS CFI DBFTFR; OpenFIGI T 3.375 09/15/28, Govt)
cases.description: United States federal government, borrowing through the U.S. Department of the Treasury. The Treasury auctions marketable debt - bills, notes with 2- to 10-year terms paying a fixed coupon every six months, bonds, inflation-protected securities and floating-rate notes - to finance federal deficits and roll over maturing public debt.
cases.nace_reasoning: Issuing debt is the state financing itself, which NACE treats as general public administration: class 84.11 explicitly covers budget implementation and management of public funds and public debt, including raising money (explanatory notes of NACE Rev. 2, p. 288, and Rev. 2.1). 'Treasury' here is a ministry, not a financial firm, so 64/66 would be wrong. Division 84 in both revisions.

BA0036 non-resident leaf 2003110 (verified). Being outside the EU (ESA S.22) does not change the BA0036 sector leaf. Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.

cases.issuer: Republic of Poland (Skarb Państwa, represented by the Minister of Finance)
cases.instrument: Republic of Poland 3.625% 11 Jan 2034, EUR 2.5bn fixed-rate EMTN bond (FIRDS CFI DTFTGB; OpenFIGI POLAND 3.625 01/11/34, Govt)
cases.description: Republic of Poland (State Treasury), represented by the Minister of Finance, who manages central government debt. It issues domestic PLN treasury securities and borrows abroad in EUR, USD and other currencies; under its Euro Medium Term Note programme it priced, for example, a EUR 2.5bn 3.625% bond due January 2034 in January 2024.
cases.nace_reasoning: Issuing debt is the state financing itself, which NACE treats as general public administration: class 84.11 explicitly covers budget implementation and management of public funds and public debt, including raising money (explanatory notes of NACE Rev. 2, p. 288, and Rev. 2.1). The Ministry of Finance is the central government body that manages the debt. Division 84 in both revisions.
cases.esa_reasoning: ESA 2010 S.1311 central government: the bond is an obligation of the Republic (State Treasury); the LEI holder is the Ministry of Finance, recorded by GLEIF as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY / CENTRAL_GOVERNMENT. BA0036 non-resident leaf 2003110 (verified). Poland being outside the euro area (ESA S.2112) does not matter for BA0036. Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.
cases.note: Traps: the GLEIF ISIN filter does not know this Eurobond (GLEIF maps only domestic PL ISINs and three CHF bonds to the Ministry's LEI), so an ISIN->GLEIF pipeline returns nothing; only FIRDS links XS2746102479 to the LEI. The XS ISIN, EMTN label and 'MINISTERSTWO FINANSÓW' name look nothing like 'Republic of Poland'.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.instrument: Land Berlin Landesschatzanweisung 2025/2030 Ausgabe 570, 2.375% 4 Jun 2030, EUR 1.5bn fixed-rate (FIRDS CFI DNFTFB; OpenFIGI BERGER 2.375 06/04/30, Govt)
cases.description: Land Berlin, Germany's capital and a city-state: one of the 16 federal states (Länder) that also performs the tasks of a municipality. Through its Senate Department for Finance it finances the state budget partly on the capital market, notably with Landesschatzanweisungen (state treasury notes), which are direct, unsecured obligations of the Land entered in its debt register.
cases.nace_reasoning: Issuing debt is the state financing itself, which NACE treats as general public administration: class 84.11 explicitly covers budget implementation and management of public funds and public debt, including raising money (explanatory notes of NACE Rev. 2, p. 288, and Rev. 2.1). 84.11 covers executive and legislative administration of central, regional and local bodies alike, so the state level changes nothing. Division 84 in both revisions.
cases.esa_reasoning: ESA 2010 S.1312 state government: GLEIF records Land Berlin as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY / STATE_GOVERNMENT, and Destatis defines the Länder level as the 13 area states plus the city-states Berlin, Bremen and Hamburg, so Berlin's municipal functions do not make it local government. The Czech name of S.1312 is 'Národní vládní instituce', hence BA0036 non-resident leaf 2003120 (verified), even though 'národní' literally reads 'national'. Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.
cases.note: Double trap: Berlin is a city, pulling towards local government (2003130), while the Czech label 'Národní vládní instituce' for S.1312 sounds like central government (2003110). Correct is state government, 2003120. The OpenFIGI ticker 'BERGER' and the German 'Land' (a federal state, not real estate) add noise.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.instrument: Ville de Paris 3.50% 5 Feb 2036, EUR 350m fixed-rate EMTN note (FIRDS CFI DTFNFB; OpenFIGI VDP 3.5 02/05/36 EMTN, Govt)
cases.description: Ville de Paris, the local authority of the French capital: since 1 January 2019 a single territorial collectivity with special status that exercises both municipal and departmental powers. Alongside bank loans it borrows on the bond market through an EMTN programme reserved for qualified investors, issuing fixed- and floating-rate notes.
cases.nace_reasoning: Issuing debt is the state financing itself, which NACE treats as general public administration: class 84.11 explicitly covers budget implementation and management of public funds and public debt, including raising money (explanatory notes of NACE Rev. 2, p. 288, and Rev. 2.1). 84.11 includes the executive administration of local bodies. Division 84 in both revisions.
cases.esa_reasoning: ESA 2010 S.1313 local government: GLEIF records the Ville de Paris as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY / LOCAL_GOVERNMENT with ELF '(Autre) Collectivité territoriale'. France has no state-government subsector, so its departmental powers do not move it to S.1312. BA0036 non-resident leaf 2003130 'Místní vládní instituce' (verified). Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.
cases.note: Traps: the capital-city name can be taken for the French Republic (central government 2003110); the departmental powers can suggest a regional level (2003120); and the EMTN programme and 'MTN' labels look corporate. Correct is local government, 2003130.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.instrument: EIB 3.875% 15 Mar 2028, USD 5bn fixed-rate global bond (FIRDS CFI DBFNGR; OpenFIGI EIB 3.875 03/15/28, Corp)
cases.description: European Investment Bank, the EU's lending institution, seated in Luxembourg and owned by the 27 EU member states. It provides loans, guarantees and advisory support for projects furthering EU policy goals such as climate action, innovation and regional cohesion, inside and outside the EU, and raises its funds by issuing bonds on international capital markets.
cases.nace_reasoning: NACE Rev. 2.1 class 99.00 covers activities of international organisations under international treaties between states (naming the IMF and the World Bank) and activities of institutions and bodies of the EU; NACE Rev. 2 class 99.00 (p. 315, same wording as ISIC Rev. 4 9900) names the IMF, the World Bank and the European Communities. The EIB is an EU body set up by the Treaties, so the classification texts put it in 99 even though its activity is lending. Alternative 64 (64.19 other monetary intermediation / 64.92 other credit granting) if CTS mirrors the ČNB treatment of the EIB as a bank (see ESA). Division 99 exists in both revisions (section U in Rev. 2, V in Rev. 2.1).
cases.esa_reasoning: In ESA 2010 the EIB is an EU body (S.2122) and an international organisation (ECB AnaCredit list: EIB, Luxembourg, code 4C); CRR art. 117(2)(j) lists it as a multilateral development bank, which would give 2009031. But the ČNB description of 2009031 says that since 2010 the EIB is, for reporting, shown among non-resident commercial banks, so the family is 'banky'. The control digit is INFERRED: 2002211 'Banky veřejné', because the EIB is owned and controlled by the governments of the member states (by analogy with resident 1221100, banks controlled by government). Q7 convention used: control is judged from the issuer's own side; an international organisation has no country of its own, so 'controlled by general government' is read as public. If CTS judges control from the Czech side (control by other states' governments = non-resident control), or reads ESA 2010 strictly (control by a foreign government = foreign-controlled), the code becomes 2002213.
cases.note: Trap: every classification rule points to 'mezinárodní rozvojové banky' (2009031) except the ČNB reporting exception, which moves the EIB to banks; and the control digit for a bank owned by 27 governments is undefined. OpenFIGI marketSector 'Corp' and the GLEIF legal-form text 'BANK' push towards an ordinary bank.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.issuer: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank)
cases.instrument: IBRD 3.875% 16 Oct 2029, USD 5bn fixed-rate global bond (FIRDS CFI DBFUGR; OpenFIGI IBRD 3.875 10/16/29, Corp)
cases.description: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the original lending institution of the World Bank Group, headquartered in Washington, D.C. and owned by 189 member countries. It lends to, guarantees and advises governments of middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and finances itself mainly by selling AAA-rated bonds on global capital markets.
cases.nace_reasoning: NACE Rev. 2.1 class 99.00 covers activities of international organisations under international treaties between states (naming the IMF and the World Bank) and activities of institutions and bodies of the EU; NACE Rev. 2 class 99.00 (p. 315, same wording as ISIC Rev. 4 9900) names the IMF, the World Bank and the European Communities. The World Bank is named explicitly, and NACE Rev. 2.1 class 64.11 even excludes 'activities of international organisations (e.g. the World Bank), see 99.00'. Alternative 64 only if CTS classifies development banks by their lending activity. Division 99 in both revisions.
cases.esa_reasoning: International organisation, non-resident of every national economy (ESA 2010 rest of the world, S.22). BA0036 splits international institutions into 2009031 'Mezinárodní rozvojové banky' (the multilateral development banks of CRR art. 117) and 2009035 'Ostatní mezinárodní instituce'. IBRD is item (a) of CRR art. 117(2) -> 2009031 (verified code). The ECB AnaCredit list of international organisations includes IBRD (code 1E). Q7 does not apply: BA0036 has no control split for government units or international institutions, so the code is the same under the own-country and the Czech-side convention.
cases.note: Trap: GLEIF's entity-supplied legal-form text says 'CENTRAL GOVERNMENT' and the legal address is in Washington, US, which invites 'US central government' (2003110) or a US bank; OpenFIGI marketSector is 'Corp'. It is a multilateral development bank: 2009031.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

Its shareholders are 77 countries together with the EU and the EIB. It invests mainly in private-sector projects, advises clients and supports policy reforms that help build market economies across three continents; it funds itself by issuing bonds.
cases.nace_reasoning: NACE Rev. 2.1 class 99.00 covers activities of international organisations under international treaties between states (naming the IMF and the World Bank) and activities of institutions and bodies of the EU; NACE Rev. 2 class 99.00 (p. 315, same wording as ISIC Rev. 4 9900) names the IMF, the World Bank and the European Communities. The EBRD is an international organisation created by an agreement between states, so it falls in 99 rather than in banking (64) despite its name. Alternative 64 if CTS classifies development banks by activity. Division 99 in both revisions.

CRR art. 117(2)(i) lists the EBRD as a multilateral development bank -> BA0036 2009031 'Mezinárodní rozvojové banky' (verified; the ČNB codelist defines 2009031 by CRR art. 117). cases.instrument: CEB 3.75% USD global notes due 14 January 2031 (issued 2026)
cases.description: Multilateral development bank of the Council of Europe, created in 1956 under a partial agreement and based in Paris, with 43 member states. It lends to member governments, local authorities and financial institutions for social projects such as housing, education, health care and support for refugees, and funds itself by issuing bonds.
cases.nace_reasoning: NACE Rev. 2 and Rev. 2.1 class 99.00 covers international organisations set up by treaties between states and names the IMF and the World Bank as examples; the CEB is such a treaty-based multilateral bank. An activity-based view gives 64 (64.92), which many commercial databases use, so the CTS convention needs confirming.
cases.esa_reasoning: International organisations are non-residents of every national economy. BA0036 item 2009031 'Mezinarodni rozvojove banky' is defined as the multilateral development banks of CRR article 117, and the CEB is named in article 117(2). The CNB reporting exception that books the EIB among non-resident banks is specific to the EIB and does not apply here. International organisations have no control split, so depends_on_q7=false.
cases.note: Legal-address trap: GLEIF shows Paris, so a country-driven rule makes it a French bank (2002211/2002212) or a French government unit, while it is an international organisation. Not to be confused with the Council of Europe itself (2009035). ESA code is high confidence; medium overall because NACE 99 vs 64 is a genuine convention question for CTS.
cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

It provides loans and other financial assistance, subject to conditions, to euro area countries facing or threatened by severe financing problems, funding itself by issuing bonds and bills.
cases.nace_reasoning: NACE Rev. 2.1 class 99.00 covers activities of international organisations under international treaties between states (naming the IMF and the World Bank) and activities of institutions and bodies of the EU; NACE Rev. 2 class 99.00 (p. 315, same wording as ISIC Rev. 4 9900) names the IMF, the World Bank and the European Communities. The ESM is an international organisation founded by a treaty between states, so 99. Alternative 64 (64.92 other credit granting) because its activity is lending to states; it takes no deposits. CRR art. 118(e) lists the ESM among international organisations, not among the art. 117 development banks -> BA0036 2009035 'Ostatní mezinárodní instituce' (verified). ECB AnaCredit list: ESM, Luxembourg, code 4S. cases.source: public sources; researched and independently re-checked on 2026-09-22; codes provisional

cases.instrument: KfW 0.05% EUR medium-term notes due 29 September 2034 (issued 2019)
cases.description: German public-law promotional bank based in Frankfurt, owned 80% by the Federal Republic and 20% by the federal states; its obligations carry a statutory federal guarantee. It finances SMEs, housing and energy efficiency, education, municipal infrastructure, export and project finance and development cooperation, funding itself mainly by issuing bonds.
cases.nace_reasoning: KfW lends (largely on-lent through commercial banks) and refinances itself with its own bonds: NACE Rev. 2 division 64 (64.19 other monetary intermediation or 64.92 other credit granting). NACE Rev. 2.1 adds a division-64 exclusion sending promotional institutions that act as the government's arm to 84.13; KfW's own-account lending as an ECB-listed credit institution is taken to stay in 64, but a Rev. 2.1 coder could argue 84.
cases.esa_reasoning: The ECB MFI list of 22 September 2026 records Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau (RIAD DE03467, same LEI) as a Credit Institution -> S.122; the CNB text of S.122 also covers units funded by continuous issuance of long-term debt securities. Destatis' EDP inventory keeps KfW outside general government and only reroutes operations KfW carries out on behalf of the federal government (placeholder share holdings, bilateral loans to Greece, special-purpose loans), so not S.13. Owned by the Federal Republic (80%) and the Länder (20%) with a statutory federal guarantee -> public. Control convention (open question Q7): control judged relative to the issuer's own country of residence, as ESA 2010 does. Controlled by German general government = 'verejne' -> 2002211 (verified CTS code). From the Czech point of view the German state is non-resident -> 2002213, hence depends_on_q7=true.
